Title: Modeling and Control of a Vehicle-to-Grid Charging Station Integrated with Wind Energy and User Participation Using MATLAB/Simulink
Source title: 2025 New Jersey Future Energy Transmission Conference, NJFET 2025
Abstract: This work presents the modeling, control, and performance evaluation of an EV charging station integrated with wind energy and the utility grid. The system comprises an off-board EV battery charger and two bidirectional charging stations that support both V2G and G2V operations under coordinated control strategies. A user-driven participation scheme, allowing EV owners to select their level of involvement based on grid conditions and personal preferences, has been developed. The proposed system was modeled and simulated in MATLAB/Simulink and experimentally validated under various scenarios, including sudden load variations, changes in user participation, and three-phase fault conditions. The results demonstrate stable DC bus voltage regulation, synchronized three-phase operation, and overall system reliability, confirming the effectiveness of the control strategy and the benefits of incorporating user participation. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Development of On-Board Navigation Software with an Interactive Interface for High-Precision Flight Trajectory Control
Source title: 2025 6th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems, CIEES 2025 - Conference Proceedings
Abstract: A software-centric on-board navigation and trajectory-control framework is presented, integrating satellite positioning, inertial sensing, Kalman filtering, and aerodynamic surface actuation within a modular architecture. A ground control station with an interactive interface (PyQt5) supports real-time monitoring, parameter tuning, and trajectory replanning. In hardware-in-the-loop simulations and bench tests, the system maintains stable performance during short GNSS interruptions (up to 5 s) and reduces dispersion (CEP proxy) from 30-40 m to 3-10 m on a legacy unguided platform surrogate under representative wind disturbances. Open architecture facilitates scalability, reproducibility, and non-weaponized research use in aerospace navigation and control. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Convergence of FPGA, Artificial Intelligence, and Synthetic Aperture Radar: A Systematic Review of Onboard Processing Architectures for Edge Intelligence
Source title: Journal of Aeronautics, Astronautics and Aviation
Abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) provides an all-weather, day-and-night remote sensing capabilities for aerospace applications. However, the large size of raw radar data creates a severe downlink bandwidth bottlenecks, necessitating an operational paradigm shift from ground-based processing to onboard edge intelligence. Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and Heterogeneous System-on-Chips (FPSoCs) have emerged as the leading hardware architectures to enable this evolution under strict Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) constraints. Using the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review widely synthesizes 49 primary studies at the convergence of FPGA, radar processing procedures, and edge deep learning optimization. This review evaluates the entire processing chain, starting from the low-level hardware mapping trade-offs of fundamental imaging algorithms, such as, Range-Doppler Algorithm (RDA), Chirp-Scaling Algorithm (CSA) and Back-Projection (BP), to the deployment of advanced radar-centric AI paradigms, such as, Complex-Valued Neural Networks (CVNNs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Quantitative benchmarking data shows that state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators achieve massive throughputs up to 9,500 FPS for 128 × 128 GNN-based target recognition tasks while model architecture co-designed CNN accelerators deliver up to a 66-fold increase in energy efficiency compared to commercial COTS CPU baselines. Furthermore, these FPGA architectures strictly adhere to tight aerospace power budgets ( < 10W ), providing a critical Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) advantage over high-power embedded GPUs. Additionally, this study critically discusses extreme aerospace environmental constraints and describes mitigation techniques for Single Event Upsets (SEU) and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) radiation effects. Finally, this paper identifies existing gaps in algorithm-hardware integration and outlines future research directions towards fully autonomous, radiation-hardened edge SAR platforms. © 2026, Journal of Aeronautics, Astronautics and Aviation. Authors: Luan X.; Eikenbroek O.A.L.; Corman F.; van Berkum E.C.
Author full names: Luan, Xiaojie (56218266600); Eikenbroek, Oskar A.L. (57197714451); Corman, Francesco (26538706900); van Berkum, Eric C. (6603222717)
Title: Passenger social rerouting strategies in capacitated public transport systems
Source title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
Abstract: Services of many public transportation systems are regulated by static timetables. Tactical decisions to improve operations are usually limited to supply-side measures that fail to quickly react to short-term changes in passenger demand and disturbances. Where the realized level of service (LoS) might be substantially different from what was expected, demand management measures, such as advising travelers to use specific routes in the interest of congestion and travel time of the entire population (social rerouting), can be implemented alongside supply-side measures to improve the LoS over different timescales. In this study, we introduce multi-modal social rerouting strategies, considering trains, buses, and trams running with predefined timetables, to improve the LoS of capacitated public transport networks by asking a portion of the passenger demand to change departure time, line, or service. In fact, we aim to balance network load by rerouting passengers using a centrally-coordinated information strategy. The strategy anticipates feedback effects due to failed boardings and discomfort because of overcrowding by incorporating behavioral responses to advice over different timescales. We explore theoretical and practical challenges by evaluating the effectiveness and performance of strategies using real-world data from the Zürich and Twente public transport networks. Numerical experiments reveal that (1) system efficiency can already be improved with the compliance of a small portion of passengers to the social rerouting advice; (2) with 20%–50% steerable passengers, the improvement gradient of system efficiency is at a maximum; (3) targeting a certain level of system efficiency, a smaller detour tolerance requires the compliance of more travelers, and a larger detour tolerance allows fewer travelers to comply with the detour. © 2024 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Ignatius T.M.; Palathinkal R.P.
Author full names: Ignatius, Titu Mary (56405560800); Palathinkal, Roy Paily (18438148100)
Title: Non-Linear Cyclic Variable Clock Feistel Bridge-Inspired Countermeasure for Securing RISC-V Crypto-Core Against Power Attacks
Source title: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I: Regular Papers
Abstract: With the increasing popularity of Internet of Things Edge (IoTe) devices, RISC-V emerges as the most suitable architecture for various applications. Since attackers have direct physical access to these IoTe devices, securing these RISC-V designs is of major concern. This research article first focuses on designing a low-power high-performance, RISC-V crypto-core for high security applications, which significantly enhances the efficiency of the AES encryption algorithm, but still susceptible to Power Analysis Attacks (PAA). A novel Non-Linear Cyclic Variable Clock Feistel Bridge-Inspired Countermeasure (NCVCFB) providing variation in both amplitude and temporal domains of signal was introduced to enhance AES security in RISC-V based IoTe devices, specially to address the vulnerability against PAA. The NCVCFB countermeasure employs the rolling architecture and will operate in tandem with each round of AES to obscure power consumption patterns. It will execute additional random number of rounds cyclically in the first and last round of AES, based on the randomly generated number. The newly designed, secured RISC-V achieved remarkably low area and power overheads of 1.05% and 1.23%, respectively, without affecting the maximum operating frequency. Nevertheless, the throughput was decreased due to variable clock count for different plaintext. The PAA was performed using the power traces captured from post-layout design on ASIC platform at UMC 65 nm technology node as well as on the experimental hardware setup employing a Side-channel Attack Security Evaluation Board (SASEBO). The resilience of the secured RISC-V architecture against PAA was tested by subjecting it to 2 Million traces, and none of the bytes got recovered. Thus, the NCVCFB secured RISC-V attained a Measurement To Disclose (MTD) >2M, Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) <0.5, Mutual Information (MI) in the milli range, and Test Vector Leakage Assessment (TVLA) within +/−4.5 limits. © 2004-2012 IEEE.

Authors: Liang L.; Lu D.; Li D.; Chen Z.; Liu S.; Wang C.; Wu X.
Title: A Biomimetic 4WS-4WD Robotic Platform with Single-Neuron PID Control for Autonomous Field Navigation
Source title: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics, ROBIO
Abstract: Autonomous navigation in unstructured agricultural environments is critical for enhancing productivity and reducing labor. This paper presents a biomimetic 4WS-4WD robotic platform with neuron-based PID control for field navigation. To improve terrain adaptability, a nonlinear elastic suspension inspired by kangaroo tendon mechanics enhances shock absorption and energy efficiency. An omnidirectional kinematic model ensures agile motion, while a single-neuron PID controller enables real-time gain tuning based on error dynamics. The system integrates GNSS-RTK, IMU, and steering encoders for centimeter-level localization. Built on ROS, the platform is validated through simulations and field tests, demonstrating robust trajectory tracking and reliable performance in diverse agricultural scenarios. All open-source materials, including CAD drawings, circuit boards, and code, can be accessed at the following repository: https://github.com/LebinLiang/four_ws_wd.  © 2025 IEEE.

Title: A High-Performance Onboard Supercapacitor ESS with SiC Power MOSFET Buck–Boost Converter for Railway Applications
Source title: Energies
Abstract: This paper is devoted to the design and implementation of a high-performance onboard Supercapacitor energy storage system (ESS) with a SiC power MOSFET-based buck–boost converter for railway applications. The SiC power MOSFET-based buck–boost converter can be switched at higher frequencies than those of Si-IGBT and Hybrid-IGBT counterparts, resulting in significant volume and cost reduction in the buck–boost inductor. A new operating strategy is proposed for a Supercapacitor ESS to optimize the electrical energy savings of a light rail transportation system (LRTS) while running on a prespecified rail track. In the Optimized Operating Strategy, regenerative braking torque and power profiles are pre-programmed before departing from each station to allow the storage of almost all of the kinetic energy of the vehicle in a Supercapacitor ESS. Details of the proposed Optimized Operating Strategy are described in a comparative manner with the Standard Operating Strategy in the paper. Furthermore, effects of the type of interface circuit between the DC catenary line and the AC grid are also discussed in view of the net energy consumption of the LRTS from the AC grid while operating on a typical rail track. All theoretical results are verified by experimental work conducted on a physical simulator. The results obtained show that an onboard Supercapacitor ESS with an Optimized Operating Strategy provides 36% energy savings with respect to the base case with no ESS of a railway vehicle moving on a prespecified track and supplied from a unidirectional interface circuit between the DC catenary and AC grid. This paper is accompanied by a video demonstrating the experimental work. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: A Fuzzy-PID controller for Minimizing the Power Fluctuation of Receiver Side of Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer System
Source title: 2025 5th IEEE International Conference on Applied Electromagnetics, Signal Processing, and Communication, AESPC 2025
Abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology is increasingly being adopted for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging due to its safety, convenience, and ability to eliminate physical connectors. However, performance degradation caused by load variations, coil misalignment, and system parameter uncertainties remains a key challenge. To further increase the range of the vehicle, a dynamic wireless power transfer(DWPT) system has been used to charge the batteries. But, the major challenges in DWPT are the intermittent charging of the batteries. This paper presents a Fuzzy-PID control approach to improve the power performance on the receiver side. In this work, a high power density super capacitor is used to energize the battery during the intermittent distance of coils. The supercapcitor with bidirectional DC-DC converter and the Fuzzy-PID controller is used to maintain a constant DC voltage across the input of the buck converter. The results are compared with a PI controller in MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation and also validated hardware platform. A 20 W system has been developed in the laboratory with the TMS28609 board to implement the Fuzzy-PID controller. The fuzzy-PID controller performs better as compared to the PI controller for this application. © 2025 IEEE.

Author full names: Chung, Min K. (61000643200); Gutierrez, Alma Maria Jennifer (18036970700); Ching, Betina (61000991300); Sol, Zian (61000847500); Sta. Cruz, Jose (61000575300); Tan, Charles (61000643300)
Title: Universal Design for the Bus Carousel in the Philippines
Source title: Industrial Engineering and Management Systems
Abstract: Public transportation systems serve as vital lifelines for urban mobility, yet they frequently fail to accommodate the diverse needs of all users, particularly older adults and persons with disabilities (PWDs). The Epifanio de los Santos Avenue (EDSA) In Metro Manila, Bus Carousel system—a high-volume dedicated median bus lane along EDSA—exemplifies this critical gap. Despite its role as a major transit artery, the system’s infrastructure presents severe accessibility and safety challenges that disproportionately impact vulnerable commuters. For this study, two groups of participants were studied. Two methods were used: naturalistic observations and interviews. Both groups consisted of daily commuters at the EDSA-Philam Bus Carousel station, encompassing a wide range of ages and physical capabilities. Moreover, observations and interviews were conducted during peak hours. Based on thorough research and results from previous studies, this study proposes the following interventions: 1. Reconfiguration of the bus layouts having left-side doors to align with the median bus lane layout and to eliminate the need for unsafe pedestrian crossings. 2. Implementation of a step-free boarding through access ramps which align wherein the slopes and height of handrails align with BP 344. Batas Pambansa Bilang 344 (BP 344), or the Accessibility Law, requires public and private buildings, educational establishments, transportation terminals, and public utilities in the Philippines to install features that enhance mobility for persons with disabilities. The proposed solutions not only improve universal design but also enhance efficiency, safety, and inclusivity for all individuals. By adopting these solutions, the EDSA Bus Carousel can evolve into a safer and more equitable transit system. © 2026 KIIE

Title: Scalable Transdiagnostic Early Assessment of Mental Health (STREAM): a study protocol
Source title: BMJ Open
Abstract: Introduction Early childhood development forms the foundations for functioning later in life. Thus, accurate monitoring of developmental trajectories is critical. However, such monitoring often relies on time-intensive assessments which necessitate administration by skilled professionals. This difficulty is exacerbated in low-resource settings where such professionals are predominantly concentrated in urban and often private clinics, making them inaccessible to many. This geographic and economic inaccessibility contributes to a significant € detection gap' where many children who might benefit from support remain undetected. The Scalable Transdiagnostic Early Assessment of Mental Health (STREAM) project aims to bridge this gap by developing an open-source, scalable, tablet-based platform administered by non-specialist workers to assess motor, social and cognitive developmental status. The goal is to deploy STREAM through public health initiatives, maximising opportunities for effective early interventions. Methods and analysis The STREAM project will enrol and assess 4000 children aged 0-6 years from Malawi (n=2000) and India (n=2000). It integrates three established developmental assessment tools measuring motor, social and cognitive functioning using gamified tasks, observation checklists, parent-report and audio-video recordings. Domain scores for motor, social and cognitive functioning will be developed and assessed for their validity and reliability. These domain scores will then be used to construct age-adjusted developmental reference curves. Ethics and dissemination Ethical approval has been obtained from local review boards at each site (India: Sangath Institutional Review Board; All India Institute of Medical Science (AIIMS) Ethics Committee; Indian Council of Medical Research - Health Ministry Screening Committee; Malawi: College of Medicine Research and Ethics Committee; Malawi Ministry of Health - Blantyre District Health Office). The study adheres to Good Clinical Practice standards and the ethical guidelines of the 6th (2008) Declaration of Helsinki. Findings from STREAM will be disseminated to participating families, healthcare professionals, policymakers, educators and researchers, at local, national and international levels through meetings, academic journals and conferences.  © 2024 BMJ Publishing Group. Authors: Fan C.; Deng Y.; Duan K.; Wang S.; Jia W.; Chen K.; Zhao J.; Jiang T.; Feng Y.
Title: Optically Transparent Metasurface for Bidirectional Wave Manipulation: Decoupling Transmission and Reflection in Multifunctional Visual-Electromagnetic Systems
Source title: Advanced Optical Materials
Abstract: Modern communication and detection platforms increasingly demand optical transparency alongside efficient microwave performance, particularly in applications of smart glass curtain walls, photovoltaic power generation, and vehicular communication systems. Optically transparent metasurfaces employ subwavelength elements to control electromagnetic (EM) wave properties, enabling dynamic beamforming, extended signal coverage, and low scattering while preserving visual clarity. However, achieving multifunctional EM control remains challenging due to material losses, restricted phase coverage, and fabrication complexities in multilayer architectures, limiting current designs to only single-mode operation (transmission or reflection) and impeding advanced integration. To address these limitations, this work proposes a transmission-reflection decoupled metasurface based on a fine metal line (FML) structure. The design enables independent, broadband, low-loss, and precise control of both transmitted and reflected EM waves. To validate this strategy, two prototype metasurface antenna arrays are designed and fabricated: a high-gain, low-scattering antenna array and a high-gain transmit-reflect antenna array. Experimental results demonstrate high optical transparency, efficient radiation performance, and broadband low-scattering characteristics. Notably, the proposed metasurfaces achieve microwave performance comparable to traditional printed circuit board (PCB)–based structures while integrating optical transparency. This study pioneers the integration of multifunctional metasurfaces with optically transparent windows, unifying microwave communication and visual interaction. © 2025 Wiley-VCH GmbH.

Authors: Liu X.; Zhao X.
Title: A Bus Rapid Transit Timetable Design Method Integrating All-Stop, Short-Turn and Limited-Stop Strategies
Source title: Promet - Traffic and Transportation
Abstract: Bus rapid transit (BRT) operates with an exclusive road environment, specialised platforms and technology-enhanced devices, which allows it to provide a higher quality of service compared with conventional bus transit. However, the temporally and spatially imbalanced distribution of passenger demand leads to a waste of BRT system investment. To improve operation efficiency, this paper presents a timetable-based optimisation method which integrates multiple operational strategies, including all-stop, short-turn and limited-stop services. A rule-based heuristic algorithm is developed to generate operational solutions for the stopping pattern and departure timetable for the analysis time period. The proposed model and algorithm enable detailed considerations of interactions among successive BRT vehicle journeys along with passengers’ boardings and alightings at stations, and the interdependencies between multiple service hours are involved. The method is validated through a real-world case study of the Fengpu Express BRT route in Shanghai, China. Sensitivity analyses are made in response to changes in OD profiles, average boarding and alighting time and maximum total mileage. Results show that the timetable-based multi-operational strategy reduces the total travel time of passengers under the same operational cost, which could facilitate future timetable design and stopping patterns of urban BRT corridors in a cost-efficient manner. © 2025, Faculty of Transport and Traffic Engineering. Title: A low-cost automatic people-counting system at bus stops using Wi-Fi probe requests and deep learning
Source title: Public Transport
Abstract: Counting people is an important part of people-centric applications, and the increase in the number of IoT devices has allowed the collection of huge amounts of data to facilitate people counting. The present study seeks to provide a novel, low-cost, automatic people-counting system for the use at bus stops, featuring a sniffing device that can capture Wi-Fi probe requests, and overcoming the problem of Media Access Control (MAC) randomization using deep learning. To make manual data collection considerably easier, a “People Counter” app was designed to collect ground truth data in order to train the model with higher accuracy. A user-friendly, operating system-independent dashboard was created to display the most relevant metrics. A two-step methodological approach was followed comprising device choice and data collection; data analysis and algorithm development. For the data analysis, three different approaches were tested, and among these a deep-learning approach using Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) with Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) architecture produced the best results. The optimal deep learning model predicted the number of people at the stop with a mean absolute error of ~ 1.2 persons, which can be considered a good preliminary result, considering that the experiment was done in a very complex open environment. People-counting systems at bus stops can support better bus scheduling, improve the boarding and alighting time of passengers, and aid the planning of integrated multi-modal transport system networks. © The Author(s) 2024.

Authors: Yu F.; Wang D.; Dai X.; Yang C.; Zhou Z.; Wang Q.
Title: Autonomous mobile off-board actuation platform for cable-driven exoskeletons: Design, control and application
Source title: Robotics and Autonomous Systems
Abstract: Cable-driven exoskeletons can effectively assist patients with neuromuscular injuries in active rehabilitation training. Off-board actuation can substantially reduce the load borne by the wearer while enabling the use of higher-power actuators, batteries, and controllers. However, existing off-board actuation systems still rely on manual operation or fixed installations, which leads to heavy manpower burden, limited overground walking, uncontrollable relative positioning, and degraded force transmission. In this paper, we propose a novel autonomous mobile off-board actuation platform specifically designed for cable-driven exoskeletons, aiming to simultaneously achieve hands-free overground mobility, high force transmission efficiency, and safety under cable constraints. The platform features a holonomic (omnidirectional) mobile architecture for formation keeping under tethered human–robot interaction, a transmission-oriented human-following protocol that maintains a fixed relative pose (a constant distance behind the wearer with a 0°orientation offset) to minimize Bowden cable bending and mitigate friction-induced efficiency loss, and a hybrid passive–active safety architecture combining a strain-compensated mechanism with an electromagnetic quick-release module to handle sudden tension and enable emergency decoupling. Moreover, a multi-sensor fusion framework together with a fuzzy-PD controller is developed for real-time 3-DOF pose estimation and robust trajectory tracking. A prototype is constructed and extensively evaluated. Experimental results demonstrate accurate following, rapid and reliable safety disengagement, and consistently high force transmission efficiency, validating the effectiveness of the proposed platform. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.
Author Keywords: Cable-driven exoskeletons; Mobile robots; Off-board actuation; Rehabilitation robots

Authors: Sulistio F.A.; Suakanto S.; Ambarsari N.; Rijadi S.C.R.
Author full names: Sulistio, Fahmi Agus (60072196200); Suakanto, Sinung (53264973800); Ambarsari, Nia (55845228800); Rijadi, Safara Cathasa Riverinda (59561165600)
Title: Detecting Fake Boarding House Listings Using Multimodal Deep Learning
Source title: Proceedings of the 2025 IEEE International Conference on Industry 4.0, Artificial Intelligence, and Communications Technology, IAICT 2025
Abstract: The increasing popularity of online boarding house rental platforms is unfortunately accompanied by a rise in fraud cases in the form of fake listings. These fake listings often display misleading text descriptions and manipulated boarding house images. Traditional manual moderation is no longer sufficient to handle the volume and complexity of these scams. To address this, we propose a multimodal deep learning model that combines textual features from Indonesia Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (IndoBERT) with visual features extracted from a Residual Network-18 (ResNet18) based Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to classify listings as real or fake. The dataset comprises 2,632 entries, consisting of 1,632 real listings and 1,000 synthetically generated fake ones, and yields a classification accuracy of 97.99%, outperforming unimodal baselines that use only text 97.15% or image 90.51% inputs. Additionally, interpretability analysis using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-Cam) highlights the model's attention to suspicious image regions, while t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-Sne) plots indicate clear separability between real and fake listings. This study fills a research gap by introducing a multimodal deep-learning approach for fraud detection in online boarding house rental platforms. The model demonstrates strong generalization across diverse fraud scenarios, highlighting its potential for broader deployment across digital property marketplaces. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Qi Z.; Zheng Y.; Li C.; Lin C.; Zhang J.; Fu Y.
Title: Deployable Vane-Type Diffuse Transmission Assembly for On-Board Calibration; [用于星上定标的叶片式可展开浸透射组件研究]
Source title: Guangxue Xuebao/Acta Optica Sinica
Abstract: Objective High-precision on-board radiometric calibration serves as the cornerstone for ensuring the quantitative application value and long-term consistency of optical remote sensing data. With the profound shift in remote sensing technology from qualitative interpretation towards precise quantitative retrieval, the performance demands placed on on-board calibration systems present unprecedented dual imperatives. On one hand, to align with the technological advancement of a new generation of large-aperture, high-resolution remote sensors, calibrators must possess full-aperture and full-optical-path calibration capabilities, which typically entail larger physical dimensions. On the other hand, the limited payload space and stringent mass budget of satellite platforms impose rigid constraints on their miniaturization and lightweight design. Furthermore, while widely used, traditional diffuse reflection panels are susceptible to space environmental contamination and performance degradation. Their alternative—fixed transmitting diffusers—though mitigating certain environmental risks, can only provide a single, fixed radiance reference. This limitation renders them incapable of performing on-orbit calibration and validation of the sensor’s radiation response linearity across its entire dynamic range, emerging as a critical bottleneck constraining the development of high-precision quantitative remote sensing. To systematically address these challenges and break through the functional and formal limitations of existing technologies, this research aims to develop a novel on-board calibration assembly that integrates exceptional compactness with multi-radiance-level output capability. Methods This paper proposed a deployable vane-type transmitting diffuser assembly as a solution. First, in terms of structural design, the assembly replaced the conventional monolithic transmitting diffuser with multiple collaboratively movable semi-crescent-shaped vanes, effectively reducing the volume of the calibration device. Second, for functional implementation, the double-layer vanes were divided into “covering layers” and “adjusting layers”, and geometric models were established to explore the influence of vane parameters on both the assembly’s radius and the variation range of the vane overlap ratio. This aimed to minimize the assembly’s size while maximizing the overlap ratio variation range, which corresponds to the transmittance radiance adjustment capability. Finally, to characterize the angular uniformity of the transmittance radiance and validate its adjustability, a prototype with a central aperture diameter of 150 mm was fabricated, and a large-aperture measurement system based on a focusing lens and angular scanning was employed to evaluate the angular distribution uniformity and dynamic adjustment range of the transmittance radiance. Results and Discussions 1) Under normal incidence condition, the fabricated assembly achieved a radiance angular uniformity of over 99% within a transmission zenith angle range of 0°–12° across 464–710 nm, meeting the optical requirements for high-precision relative radiometric calibration. This performance was superior to the 95% angular uniformity of monolithic transmitting diffusers, indicating that the proposed structure enhances angular uniformity. 2) Under oblique incidence conditions, the angular uniformity of radiance for the component within the –12° to 12° transmission angle range at 710 nm decreased with increasing incidence zenith angle and showed a strong dependence on the incidence azimuth angle. The performance was optimal within a certain range, reaching 98% at an incidence zenith angle of 30°. The relationship between angular uniformity and incidence zenith angle was influenced by the component’s structure, thereby determining the installation orientation constraints for the component within the sensor integration. 3) By adjusting the vane overlap ratio, the transmittance radiance of the assembly could be continuously and smoothly regulated between 75% and 100% of its maximum value, validating the multi-level radiometric calibration capability of this structure. Analysis based on the geometric model of the vane overlap ratio variation range suggests that a larger vane width could further extend the adjustment range to 50%–100% of the maximum transmittance radiance. 4) The geometric models of the assembly radius and vane overlap ratio variation range reveal a design trade-off between the radial size and the dynamic range of transmittance radiance. When multi-level radiometric calibration is not considered, the assembly’s radius was reduced compared to traditional calibration wheel structures, and the fabricated prototype remained more compact than conventional calibration wheel designs. Compared to existing transmitting diffuser solutions, this work not only achieves advancements in miniaturization but also enables multi-radiance-level radiometric calibration within a certain range, offering new insights for on-board radiometric calibration. Conclusions This study successfully designed and validated a deployable vane-type transmitting diffuser assembly. Through structural innovation, the assembly effectively addresses the dual requirements of compactness and radiance adjustability in on-board calibration systems. Experimental results demonstrate its reliable dynamic adjustment capability for transmittance radiance while maintaining high optical uniformity. This research provides a feasible technical pathway for the development of next-generation on-board calibration systems. Subsequent efforts will be dedicated to the refinement of the component’s mechanical structure and to the study of its performance stability in a space environment. © 2026, Chinese Laser Press. All rights reserved.
Author Keywords: angular uniformity; deployable vanes; diffuse transmission assembly; multi-radiance level; on-board calibration

Authors: Daniel Vazquez-Gasca B.; Morales-Caporal R.; Malaquias Quintero-Flores P.; Bonilla-Huerta E.; Arjona M.A.
Author full names: Daniel Vazquez-Gasca, Brayan (60823447900); Morales-Caporal, Roberto (25654128400); Malaquias Quintero-Flores, Perfecto (60823588500); Bonilla-Huerta, Edmundo (56002758300); Arjona, Marco A. (6701484173)
Title: IoT Cloud-Based Portable Power Quality Monitoring System With Dual-Path Wireless Communication
Source title: IEEE Access
Abstract: This paper presents the development and validation of an IoT cloud-based portable Power Quality Monitoring (PQM) system for low-voltage three-phase and single-phase electrical distribution networks. The design phase integrated the set of parameters and aggregation procedures specified in the IEC 61000-4-30 standard for Class S statistical surveys. The printed circuit board developed for the portable PQM system also adheres to the IPC-2221B and IEC 60664-1 design standards, with a documented galvanic isolation barrier between the power grid interface and the digital processing stage. The measured parameters include RMS voltages and currents, phasor diagram, phase angles between the signals, phase frequency, active, reactive, and apparent power, power factor, VTHD, ITHD, voltage and current unbalance, voltage sags, swells, interruptions, and device deployment location. The portable PQM is powered by the power network being monitored; in the event of a power outage, it automatically switches to an integrated backup battery, guaranteeing uninterrupted measurement and data transmission. The acquired data are transmitted to an IoT cloud platform via Wi-Fi or 4G LTE using the MQTT protocol, with automatic failover between routes. An SD card buffers data when connectivity is lost and retransmits them chronologically once connectivity is restored. Laboratory experimental tests conducted with a three-phase AC induction motor and a single-phase nonlinear load showed measurement agreement within 1 % with respect to a Class S commercial power quality analyzer for all electrical parameters analyzed. Furthermore, it was verified that no measurement records were lost during communication failure tests or power outages. © 2013 IEEE.

Authors: Ravelo B.; Guerin M.; Rahajandraibe W.
Author full names: Ravelo, Blaise (22036080600); Guerin, Mathieu (36680121800); Rahajandraibe, Wenceslas (24462065900)
Title: Accelerometer Sensed Moving Object Position Real-Time Prediction with Arduino-Embedding Negative Group Delay Function
Source title: IEEE Sensors Journal
Abstract: An innovative application of negative group delay (NGD) circuit embedded in a mobile platform for the real-time prediction of arbitrarily moving object position is developed in this article. The study case is constituted by a scenario of mini-vehicle moving in go-and-back (GAB) along a straight trajectory equipped by a commercial accelerometer sensor associated with an NGD digital circuit. The instantaneous position generated by the accelerometer sensor is considered an input signal having an arbitrary waveform to be predicted by the NGD circuit. The design method of embedded NGD digital circuit is described as a function of the targeted time advance of moving object position to be predicted. The design equations for calculating the NGD predictor parameters are formulated. Furthermore, the routine methodology of the NGD predictor algorithm is elaborated. The prediction function was implemented into the Arduino UNO platform embedded in the mobile object as an experimental demonstration for the feasibility study. To validate the innovative predictor, a mini-vehicle prototype embedding the NGD function into the Arduino board is arbitrarily moved in GAB by comparing the directly measured sensed and predicted instantaneous positions. The test is based on the mini-vehicle arbitrary random movement along a straight rectilinear track having more than 10 cm in length with a velocity of less than 0.2 m/s. By using the NGD predictor, the real-time prediction of the mini-vehicle position with -80-ms time advance is confirmed by a good agreement between the theory and experiment. The developed NGD predictor is useful for the sensor design and industrial engineering by reducing the error of teleautomatic and robotic system victim of undesirable signal propagation delays. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Jia Y.; Chen Q.; Fu L.; Zhang Y.; Zhu T.; Shi Y.; Li H.
Title: Modeling and simulation of alighting and boarding processes of passengers in metro stations
Source title: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
Abstract: Subway efficiency is significantly affected by chaotic boarding and alighting processes. A modified Social Force Model (MSFM) is proposed to address this issue. The “Disembarking Precedes Embarking” (DPE) rule is integrated with microscopic mechanisms, such as body rotation and obstacle avoidance. Simulations are conducted using realistic spatial configurations. The model is validated against experimental data, and no significant difference is shown. Consequently, realistic passenger dynamics are effectively captured. It is observed that operation times are prolonged by non-compliance with the DPE rule of pedestrians. Furthermore, door congestion is maximized at a 1:1 boarding-to-alighting ratio. A strategy allowing alighting from the center and boarding from both sides is proven to be superior. This research will provide theoretical support for the design of public transit facilities and practical guidance strategies to enhance passenger flow and safety. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Tan C.; Liu W.; Zhu C.; Tan W.; Sun M.; Zhang X.
Title: A Detection Method for Metal Plate Surface Defects Based on an Array Flat Plates Capacitive Sensor
Source title: IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Magazine
Abstract: To effectively identify and locate the surface defects of the metal plates, this research proposed a detection method based on an array flat plates capacitive sensor. To study the electric field distributions of the surface defect on metal plates and the potential difference of the induction electrode pairs, a mathematical model used to detect the surface defects of the metal plates was established in COMSOL. Based on the established model, the parameters of the PCB sensor layout were optimized, and the impact factors of the defect detection were studied. To accurately identify and locate the position of the defects, three-dimensional and two-dimensional images were made using the measured data of six different defect shapes. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, a non-destructive testing platform including eight-channel capacitor electrodes on PCB signal condition circuit and sampling system was developed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can rapidly, conveniently and effectively detect and locate surface defects on metal plates.  © 1998-2012 IEEE.

Authors: Zhuo S.; Zhu X.; Shang P.; Liu Z.; Liao F.
Author full names: Zhuo, Siyu (58112725000); Zhu, Xiaoning (8051528100); Shang, Pan (56708208600); Liu, Zhengke (57568105000); Liao, Feixiong (36876589400)
Title: Joint optimization of fleet size and operating speed for service planning in oversaturated urban rail transit networks
Source title: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review
Abstract: Oversaturated operations have become increasingly common in urban rail transit (URT) systems, where peak-period passenger demand often exceeds available service capacity. This demand–capacity imbalance leads to platform queues, in-train crowding, and denied boarding, making service planning particularly challenging when fleet resources are limited. To address the coupled supply–demand interactions, this study proposes a novel Behavior–Energy-Adaptive Service planning (BEAS) framework for network-wide URT service planning, in which fleet allocation and line-level operating speed are jointly optimized while passengers’ adaptive route choices are explicitly modeled. An integrated nonlinear integer programming model is developed to link fleet–speed service-plan decisions, subject to fleet budget limits and speed-dependent traction energy costs, with passenger assignment and path-size logit (PSL)-based route choice in a capacity-constrained space–time network. By enforcing train capacity and first-in-first-out (FIFO) boarding, the model reproduces platform queueing and denied boarding, and captures how the resulting time-dependent travel costs drive adaptive rerouting under oversaturated conditions. To solve the resulting large-scale coupled problem, a decomposition-based iterative algorithm is developed, in which the demand-side subproblem simulates individual passenger assignment under time-dependent costs and the supply-side subproblem optimizes fleet and speed decisions through an incremental approximation that yields a tractable multiple-choice knapsack structure. Numerical experiments on both a small illustrative network and a large-scale Beijing metro network demonstrate the computational efficiency, scalability, and practical value of the proposed framework. The results show that coordinated fleet–speed service planning can substantially reduce waiting time and left-behind passengers under resource constraints, while supporting passenger-oriented, operator-oriented, and balanced service planning. © 2026 The Authors.
Author Keywords: Adaptive route choices; Fleet allocation; Operating speed; Oversaturated operations; Urban rail transit networks

Authors: Das A.; Bose S.; Jain R.K.

Title: MQTT Protocol Based Real-Time Operation in Mobile Robotic System Using IoT Technique
Source title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Computer, Electronics, Electrical Engineering and their Applications, IC2E3 2025
Abstract: This paper proposes an IoT-enabled mobile robotic system using the MQTT cloud platform for remote monitoring and control system in real-Time wirelessly where the robotic control system is designed with the help of MQTT protocol in IoT cloud platform, ESP32 CAM and IoT gateway where MQTT protocol provides the bi-directional communication using publish and subscribe the data within ESP32 CAM microcontroller and robot. The MQTT broker is also applied for subscribing to one or more topics to the clients such as PC/mobile phone using android/web application and will receive messages from those topics once subscribed which is a major advantage of the application of MQTT protocol in IoT Technique. ESP32 CAM is also used for monitoring the environment because it has a built-in wireless camera, ESP 32 microcontroller, and a wi-fi shield with a low-cost single board. It also takes less power consumption and communication time during real-Time operation. An experimental prototype is also developed. By demonstration, the experiment result shows the viability of implementing the MQTT cloud platform into wireless remote control robots using the IoT cloud platform for monitoring and inspection systems. During data transmission, the packet size is less than the HTTP protocol. The signal strength of wireless communication is also analyzed which helps in long-range wireless communications. Therefore, this IoT-enabled mobile robotic system proves an effective tool for real-Time monitoring and rapid wireless communication. It provides an impact and is highly valuable in a wide range of robotic applications.  © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Wouters J.; De Roose J.; Dekkers G.; Demeyer P.-J.; De Vos L.; Ivashkovych X.; Beusen B.; Luyts A.; Livens S.; Nuyts D.; Rajappa A.J.; Cassimon T.; Delauré B.; Geelen B.; Matthijs P.; Willems R.; Vanden Bussche S.; Cao Y.; Desoete B.; Van Achteren T.; Reiter P.; Tack K.; Ramos J.P.
Title: MOVIQ: AN END-TO-END APPROACH TO ENABLE HIGH-RESOLUTION HYPERSPECTRAL VISION INTELLIGENCE ON BOARD SATELLITES
Source title: Proceedings of SPIE - The International Society for Optical Engineering
Abstract: Recent advancements in technology have led to the development of smaller instruments, sensors, and electronics, enabling small satellite systems to collect vast amounts of data at a relatively low cost. This has sparked significant growth in the private Earth observation (EO) industry. Despite the deployment of satellite constellations with improved spectral, spatial, and temporal resolutions, there remains a bottleneck in data transmission and downlink capabilities, hindering efficient information extraction. Emerging technologies in artificial intelligence (AI), inter-satellite communication, and edge processing are promising to address these challenges, revolutionizing satellite missions and operations. The integration of intelligent payloads in various recent satellite demonstrators is marking progress towards autonomous satellite constellations. To meet the growing demand for autonomous and intelligent remote sensing, initiatives like the MOVIQ project are crucial. MOVIQ aims to enhance data processing efficiency and advance EO capabilities through agile satellite platforms, high-resolution optical payloads, fault-tolerant AI processors, advanced applications and streamlined integration and optimization frameworks. These efforts promise to deliver cost-effective, intelligent mission platforms capable of real-time situational awareness and application-specific insights to further drive innovation in the EO sector. © 2025 The Authors.

Authors: Gavriilidis N.O.; Halkidis S.T.; Petridou S.
Author full names: Gavriilidis, Nikolaos Orestis (59964155100); Halkidis, Spyros T. (14048443900); Petridou, Sophia (14038067400)
Title: Empirical Evaluation of TLS-Enhanced MQTT on IoT Devices for V2X Use Cases
Source title: Applied Sciences (Switzerland)
Abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) deployment has led to an unprecedented volume of interconnected, resource-constrained devices. Securing their communication is essential, especially in vehicular environments, where sensitive data exchange requires robust authentication, integrity, and confidentiality guarantees. In this paper, we present an empirical evaluation of TLS (Transport Layer Security)-enhanced MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) on low-cost, quad-core Cortex-A72 ARMv8 boards, specifically the Raspberry Pi 4B, commonly used as prototyping platforms for On-Board Units (OBUs) and Road-Side Units (RSUs). Three MQTT entities, namely, the broker, the publisher, and the subscriber, are deployed, utilizing Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) for key exchange and authentication and employing the AES_256_GCM and ChaCha20_Poly1305 ciphers for confidentiality via appropriately selected libraries. We quantify resource consumption in terms of CPU utilization, execution time, energy usage, memory footprint, and goodput across TLS phases, cipher suites, message packaging strategies, and both Ethernet and WiFi interfaces. Our results show that (i) TLS 1.3-enhanced MQTT is feasible on Raspberry Pi 4B devices, though it introduces non-negligible resource overheads; (ii) batching messages into fewer, larger packets reduces transmission cost and latency; and (iii) ChaCha20_Poly1305 outperforms AES_256_GCM, particularly in wireless scenarios, making it the preferred choice for resource- and latency-sensitive V2X applications. These findings provide actionable recommendations for deploying secure MQTT communication on an IoT platform. © 2025 by the authors.

Authors: Choubey N.; Patil V.; Verma A.

Title: Private SUV or Carpooling?—Investigating Impact of Choices on Indian Roads
Source title: Lecture Notes in Civil Engineering
Abstract: There is an increasing tendency to buy bigger cars, especially SUVs, as a status quo symbol. Automobile companies observed an increased demand this year. This is likely to aggravate the already congested roads in most Indian metropolitan cities. Many signalized intersections are experiencing long queues and longer waiting times. Unlike public transport, which carries more passengers for the space it occupies, SUVs have a lower vehicle occupancy. Many studies have been conducted on SUVs based on the safety, environment aspects while there is a gap in studying the impact of SUVs on traffic. This study proposes an impact assessment of the penetration of SUVs through simulations. Vehicle pooling is also assessed as an alternative. The study has been conducted on Silk Board junction in Bangalore with peak hour and off-peak hour traffic. It was observed that up to 3 min in peak and 4 min in non-peak hour per vehicle for a 4 km ride can be saved if all cars are pooled while up to 2 min in peak and 5 min in non-peak hour per vehicle can be saved if only SUVs are pooled for the same journey. The results showcase that penalizing buying private SUVs as a mode of transport and incentivizing carpooling or adopting high occupancy vehicles to make them a lucrative option need to be done to improve the overall sustainability of urban transport. The study could help the policymakers to address the issue of this new trend of buying bigger private cars such as SUVs. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2024.

Authors: Lv B.; Li X.; Hao B.; Chen Q.
Title: Estimating bus boarding stops under missing key fields in smart card transaction data
Source title: Applied Intelligence
Abstract: This study proposes a hybrid framework to estimate boarding stops in public transit systems using smart card and GPS data, addressing the absence of key fields like vehicle IDs and stop identifiers in entry-only systems. A time-window matching algorithm links transactions to potential stops, followed by passenger classification into high- and low-frequency groups. For frequent travelers, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) leverages travel chains for accurate inference, while an enhanced k-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm predicts stops for infrequent travelers using spatiotemporal proximity. Evaluated on Lanzhou’s Route 80 and Route 77 (June 2023), the method demonstrates high consistency (with cosine similarity exceeding 0.91) and achieves well-balanced passenger flows, with balance coefficients of 0.97 and 0.89. Field surveys confirm alignment with observed patterns at key hubs. This scalable approach is well-suited to urban transit systems with limited data integration, supporting improved planning and operational optimization. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2025.

Authors: Chen B.; Tan L.; Li P.; Tan L.; Wang H.; Chen C.
Title: A robust nonlinear model-based controller design for a hybrid wave compensation boarding platform for offshore wind farm operation and maintenance
Source title: Ocean Engineering
Abstract: This paper presents a nonlinear extended state observer (NLESO) based nonlinear model predictive controller (NMPC) design for a redundant 9-degree-of-freedom hybrid wave compensation boarding platform for offshore wind farm operation and maintenance to compensate for wave-induced vessel motions. The proposed NLESO is designed to estimate the total disturbance acting on the platform, which arises from unknown variations induced by wind, waves, currents, and the dynamic coupling within the redundant system. First, a task-priority motion planning method dynamically generates the desired compensation trajectory for the hybrid boarding platform to track. Simultaneously, the dynamic model of the hybrid wave compensation platform is transformed into a form suitable for designing the NLESO. Subsequently, the estimated disturbances and the desired compensation trajectory are incorporated into the NMPC to achieve the intended compensation for the platform. The stability of the proposed NLESO based NMPC is analyzed by representing the entire coupled system in the form of a Lure system. Following this, simulation verification demonstrates that, compared to Linear Extended State Observer based Model Predictive Controller (LESO-MPC), Sliding Mode Control (LESO-SMC), and Backstepping Control methods (LESO-Backstepping) under external disturbances, the proposed control strategy achieves lower trajectory tracking errors. Consequently, the wave compensation boarding platform exhibits excellent stability and high control accuracy during coordinated wave compensation tasks. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Zheng Z.; Rao C.; Zhang X.; Lu L.; Zhang X.; Wei H.; Lou X.
Title: Unity-EDR: A Hybrid Neural-Mesh Rendering System for Efficient Visual Synthesis
Source title: Proceedings - IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
Abstract: Neural rendering delivers photorealistic visual quality but remains computationally prohibitive for interactive applications. To overcome this bottleneck, we propose a real-time neural-raster fusion system that integrates neural and mesh-based rendering for efficient visual synthesis. The architecture adopts a screen-aligned fusion strategy that shares an optical center and field-of-view, enabling direct alpha blending of RGBA frames without incurring depth exchange, calibration, or warping overhead. A lightweight, multi-threaded server utility enables asynchronous communication with a neural rendering coprocessor named EDR-NR, effectively decoupling hardware rendering from the Unity host. In addition, an efficient ray-marched shadow casting method leverages the EDR-NR's native hierarchical fine grid data structure for real-time soft-shadow approximation. Evaluation results demonstrate the system's efficiency and seamless compatibility with standard rendering pipelines. The quad-core EDR-NR prototype implemented on an FPGA board, integrated with Unity, achieves over 200 frames per second (FPS) on the chair dataset within a mesh-based scene, demonstrating that practical, high-speed neural rendering on edge platforms is fully achievable within a commercial game engine environment. © 2026 IEEE.

Authors: Notarianni L.; Bagnato R.; Sabatini A.; Tomaso G.D.; Vollero L.
Author full names: Notarianni, Luca (60102472100); Bagnato, Roberto (60102699500); Sabatini, Anna (57204781629); Tomaso, Giulia Di (58538960100); Vollero, Luca (8579534700)
Title: Storage I/O Characterization for an Embedded Multi-Sensor Platform: Performance Bottlenecks and Design Guidelines
Source title: Electronics (Switzerland)
Abstract: Microcontroller-based embedded systems integrating multiple sensors are increasingly required to support continuous data acquisition, on-board processing, and long-term storage within tightly coupled hardware–software architectures. In such platforms, overall performance is often constrained not by computational capability but by storage I/O behavior, particularly under real-time constraints and concurrent workloads. This study presents a comprehensive empirical evaluation of eMMC storage performance on an STM32U5 microcontroller running the ThreadX RTOS. The proposed methodology combines multi-dimensional stress testing, controlled task concurrency (0–4 tasks), and long-duration aging analysis (90 h), together with timing variability assessment under electrical stress and interrupt-driven preemption. Both synthetic workloads and realistic sensor-node scenarios with heterogeneous and asynchronous access patterns are considered. The results highlight significant performance limitations, including up to 98% throughput degradation under four concurrent tasks and a nonlinear increase in metadata latency as free space decreases below 40% (from 10 ms to over 200 ms for file creation). Additionally, timing jitter increases by 2–5× under voltage variation and interrupt load. Based on these findings, practical firmware-level design guidelines are derived, including sector-aligned buffering, dedicated I/O task architectures, and proactive capacity management, enabling substantial improvements in throughput and latency. This study provides quantitative insights and reproducible methodologies for optimizing storage subsystems in multi-sensor embedded applications. © 2026 by the authors.
Author Keywords: benchmarking; embedded systems; eMMC; FileX; flash memory; microcontrollers; RTOS; storage characterization

Authors: Guo S.; Zhang W.; Zheng Y.; Li H.; Yang Y.; Xu J.
Title: Research on the Lossless Data Compression System of the Argo Buoy Based on BiLSTM-MHSA-MLP
Source title: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
Abstract: This study addresses the issues of the limited data storage capacity of Argo buoys and satellite communication charges on the basis of data volume by proposing a block lossless data compression method that combines bidirectional long short-term memory networks and multi-head self-attention with a multilayer perceptron (BiLSTM-MHSA-MLP). We constructed an Argo buoy data compression system using the main buoy control board, Jetson nano development board, and the BeiDou-3 satellite transparent transmission module. By processing input sequences bidirectionally, BiLSTM enhances the understanding of the temporal relationships within profile data, whereas the MHSA processes the outputs of the BiLSTM layer in parallel to obtain richer representations. Building on this preliminary probability prediction model, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a block length parameter (block_len) are introduced to achieve block compression during training, dynamically updating the model and optimizing symbol probability distributions for more accurate predictions. Experiments conducted on multiple 4000 m single-batch profile datasets from both the PC and Jetson nano platforms demonstrate that this method achieves a lower compression ratio, shorter compression time, and greater specificity. This approach significantly reduces the communication time between Argo buoys and satellites, laying a foundation for the future integration of Jetson Nano into Argo buoys for real-time data compression. © 2024 by the authors.

Authors: Li H.; Kim S.
Title: Efficient Route Planning for Real-Time Demand-Responsive Transit
Source title: Computers, Materials and Continua
Abstract: Demand Responsive Transit (DRT) responds to the dynamic users’ requests without any fixed routes and timetables and determines the stop and the start according to the demands. This study explores the optimization of dynamic vehicle scheduling and real-time route planning in urban public transportation systems, with a focus on bus services. It addresses the limitations of current shared mobility routing algorithms, which are primarily designed for simpler, single origin/destination scenarios, and do not meet the complex demands of bus transit systems. The research introduces an route planning algorithm designed to dynamically accommodate passenger travel needs and enable real-time route modifications. Unlike traditional methods, this algorithm leverages a queue-based, multi-objective heuristic A∗ approach, offering a solution to the inflexibility and limited coverage of suburban bus routes. Also, this study conducts a comparative analysis of the proposed algorithm with solutions based on Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm (ACO), focusing on calculation time, route length, passenger waiting time, boarding time, and detour rate. The findings demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly enhances route planning speed, achieving an 80–100-fold increase in efficiency over existing models, thereby supporting the real-time demands of Demand-Responsive Transportation (DRT) systems. The study concludes that this algorithm not only optimizes route planning in bus transit but also presents a scalable solution for improving urban mobility. © 2024 Tech Science Press. Authors: Zheng Q.; Huang C.; Chen P.; Liu J.; Luo Q.; Li Y.; Liu S.; Yi J.; Wang Z.; Dai J.S.
Title: A Vision-Based Pose-Adjustment Soft Surface With Backlit Illumination for Multiadaptive Inspection
Source title: IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
Abstract: Electronics inspection in production and maintenance lines faces distinct challenges. Fixed-focus imaging thrives in standardized production layouts but faces challenges with unpredictable irregularities in maintenance lines, such as component layouts and geometries. To address this, researchers explored adaptive platforms, particularly soft programmable surfaces for pose control. However, most existing solutions rely on light-sensitive feedback, and lack passive adaptability and integrated backlit illumination, which limits their effectiveness. This article introduces the villi-like adaptive leveling and backlit illumination soft surface (VALBS), a soft robotic platform that integrates passive compliance, active pneumatic three degree of freedom pose control, and embedded backlit illumination, enabling robust inspection without altering camera hardware. Building on this, the soft actuated multiadaptive inspection (SAMI) platform is constructed, comprising a 2 × 2 array of VALBS units. Each VALBS adjusts the object’s pose through pneumatic actuation, guided by an analytical control model and visual feedback. Experiments show SAMI achieves 100% contour detection accuracy and 85% –100% pose adjustment success rate on five representative layouts pattern of printed circuit board assembly along with a range of commercially available mainboards, validating the platform’s effectiveness in handling geometric and lighting condition variability in maintenance-line inspection. © 1996-2012 IEEE. All rights reserved.

Authors: Buragadda S.; Durga G.B.S.N.; Varma S.K.; Subhani Sk.M.

Title: Advanced Fake News Detection System with Board Natural Language Processing with Rich Feature Engineering
Source title: Proceedings of 4th International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems, ICSSAS 2026
Abstract: The quick dissemination of wrong information by digital platforms has created a pressing task in detecting fake news, as misleading content has the potential to sway general opinion and choices. The currently used methods in detecting fake news are not adept at comprehending deep levels of meaning in reports are not proficient in dealing with articles in other languages and are not transparent in their prediction explanations. Against this background, this research presents an innovative method in detecting fake news that incorporates the concept of bidirectional natural language processing, extensive feature development and explainable artificial intelligence. The innovative method will start by gathering genuine and fake pieces of news from a variety of authentic sources to promote diversity in the data sets. Intensive text processing will also be used to boost the quality of the text by performing normalization, cleaning and stemming. Semantic mappings will also be created using a contextual embedding model at the sentence level to promote meaning extraction in the text. Finally, a bidirectional transformer classification model will be used to differentiate authentic from fake pieces of news by leveraging context in both directions. To enable practical usability, the proposed system incorporates a user interface that accepts news input in any language through automatic language detection and translation processes performed before prediction. It generates class labels and corresponding prediction probabilities improving interpretability. Moreover, entity highlight text for interpretability is also incorporated to offer explanations for prediction results. Experimentations performed show that the proposed technique is reliable having a training accuracy of 99.19% and testing accuracy of 97.338% which is a remarkable value for accuracy. The proposed technique is accurate, multilingual and has explanations for fake news prediction making it practical. © 2026 IEEE.

Authors: Namani R.; Subramaniam S.; Samikannu S.; Gurusamy M.

Title: A simple control strategy and dynamic energy management for the operation of combined grid-connected and standalone solar photovoltaic applications
Source title: Journal of King Saud University - Engineering Sciences
Abstract: There is an increased focus on energy savings in low-voltage DC (LVDC) loads for home appliances. The use of LVDC for the local distribution system enables easier integration with renewable sources. This work presents the control and management of power flow to DC loads in grid-tied photovoltaic (GPV) systems. This system provides bi-directional flow of power from the DC load to the AC grid, using a pulse width modulation (PWM) technique, employing a voltage source inverter between the DC nano grid and the AC main grid. The bidirectional converter controls the active power transferred in both directions while operating at unity power factor (UPF). The modified three-level hysteresis current controller and the voltage controller are designed as the inner loop and the outer loop, respectively, to control the bi-directional power flow. The corresponding grid voltages and currents are used to generate the reference currents. The proposed system has been validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations and experimentation on a prototype system developed in the laboratory controlled by the dSPACE 1103 real-time digital controller board. The results show that a regulated DC voltage is obtained for dynamic changes of source and load like in a real-time environment. The control strategy with its validation shows the efficacy of the proposed system. © 2021 The Authors

Title: First Detection of Firework-Generated Infrasound in the Upper Mesosphere–Lower Thermosphere With a Rocket-Borne Sensor: Results From the MOMO3 Sounding Rocket Experiment
Source title: Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
Abstract: We present the first direct detection of firework-generated infrasound in the upper mesosphere and lower thermosphere using a rocket-borne sensor. A wideband capacitive differential pressure sensor (INF03D) was installed on board the MOMO3 sounding rocket, a privately developed vehicle launched from Taiki, Hokkaido, Japan, in May 2019, which reached a maximum altitude of ∼113 km. Ten spherical fireworks were launched from the ground before and after liftoff to provide temporally tagged acoustic sources. Here, (Formula presented.) denotes the rocket launch time ((Formula presented.) s), and all time stamps are given relative to launch unless otherwise stated. Three-dimensional ray-tracing simulations were performed with four atmospheric profile sets (NRLMSISE-00/HWM14, JAWARA, ERA5, and MERRA-2) to evaluate spatiotemporal intersections between acoustic ray paths and the rocket trajectory. Four distinct pressure transients with Hilbert-envelope amplitudes of 1.0–2.8 Pa were detected at 50–76 km during ascent, falling within the modeled arrival windows for the T-30 s and T-90 s shots. In addition, two weak peaks (∼3.8 mPa each) were observed at 106–109 km during descent, coinciding with a predicted intersection window and classified as marginal hits due to their limited signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). Additional ascent-phase transients around T+170–T+185 s lacked corresponding ray–rocket intersections, suggesting unmodeled propagation or non-firework sources, and telemetry loss after T+282 s prevented evaluation of late-descent signals. These findings demonstrate that 0.1–2 Hz infrasound from near-surface explosions can propagate to over 100 km altitude and that rocket-borne sensors provide an effective platform for in situ acoustic measurements in the middle and upper atmosphere. © 2026. Authors: Kim D.J.H.; Joe I.
Author full names: Kim, Daniel Jin Hun (57358139400); Joe, Inwhee (56212559100)
Title: Risk-Aware Scheduling and Placement for Bus-Stop Wireless Powered Communication Networks
Source title: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
Abstract: Scheduled electric buses can serve as mobile hybrid access points (HAPs) for bus-stop wireless powered communication networks (WPCNs), providing short energy-transfer and uplink opportunities to low-power passenger-carried devices waiting outside the bus. We consider a brief uplink before boarding; after the passenger boards, the corresponding device leaves the modeled bus-stop user set. Some devices may therefore end up with low terminal accumulated throughput, making lower-tail fairness a central design concern. Addressing this risk requires per-stop decisions: selecting users, choosing curbside bus placement, and allocating dwell time between downlink wireless power transfer and uplink information transmission. We formulate this as a stochastic multi-stage mixed-integer nonlinear program maximizing a Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) objective over terminal accumulated user throughputs. To make the problem tractable, we propose a two-layer method: the Projected CVaR-tail selector (PCVaR-tail) for sparse lower-tail-aware user selection, followed by sequential least-squares quadratic programming for continuous placement and time allocation. Across ten traffic regimes, PCVaR-tail improves held-out global CVaR over the strongest Fixed- p heuristic by 3.1%, 10.1%, and 14.1% at α =0.25, 0.10, and 0.05, respectively. Additional baselines, stress tests, high-load scenarios, and trajectory diagnostics show that PCVaR-tail provides a practical, interpretable lower-tail fairness mechanism for scheduled-bus WPCNs. © 2017 IEEE.
Author Keywords: conditional value-at-risk; electric buses; lower-tail fairness; mixed-integer nonlinear programming; mobile hybrid access points; placement and time allocation; user scheduling; Wireless powered communication networks

Authors: Xiao Y.; Wang F.
Title: Edge-Cloud Collaborative IoT System Architecture and its Reliable Transmission Mechanism for Geological Disaster Monitoring
Source title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Electronic Information, Computer and Aerospace Remote Sensing, EICARS 2026
Abstract: Aiming at the critical problems of high data transmission latency, highly vulnerable communication links, and overwhelming processing loads on central servers inherent in traditional geological disaster monitoring systems deployed in complex mountainous environments, an advanced edge-cloud collaborative Internet of Things system architecture alongside a highly reliable heterogeneous transmission mechanism is proposed. First, a comprehensive four-layer Internet of Things architecture comprising the perception, network, platform, and application layers is meticulously designed to establish clear functional boundaries and operational continuity. An innovative edge-cloud collaborative processing mechanism is introduced, wherein distributed edge computing nodes, utilizing ultra-lowpower microcontrollers and capable single-board computers, perform the immediate initial filtering of multi-source sensor data, rigorous outlier removal, and localized threshold-based early warning generation. This decentralization dramatically reduces upstream transmission bandwidth requirements and localized response latency. Concurrently, the centralized cloud platform leverages sophisticated multi-sensor data fusion algorithms and complex physical models to conduct in-depth historical data mining and comprehensive global risk assessments. Second, targeting the fundamental pain point of extreme network instability in rugged topographies, a reliable transmission network based primarily on heterogeneous Low-Power Wide-Area Networks, incorporating both Long Range and Narrowband Internet of Things technologies, is engineered with multi-communication backup mechanisms and dynamic failover logic. Additionally, the lightweight Message Queuing Telemetry Transport protocol, combined with localized payload encryption and adaptive data compression algorithms, is deployed at the transmission layer. This strategic protocol optimization ensures secure, high-throughput, and energy-efficient data transmission in the harshest of environmental conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive hybrid transmission strategy achieves packet delivery ratios of 99.5%-99.9% over transmission distances of 2-10 km. Meanwhile, the edge-cloud collaborative architecture reduces the end-to-end response time to 0.97-3.65 across the evaluated event types. These results verify that the proposed architecture can effectively improve transmission reliability and real-time warning performance in complex mountainous environments.  © 2026 IEEE.
Author Keywords: Edge-Cloud Collaboration; Geological Disaster Monitoring; Internet of Things; Low-Power Wide-Area Network; Message Queuing Telemetry Transport; Reliable Transmission

Authors: Pei H.; Fan Q.; Duan Y.; Xiao L.
Author full names: Pei, Hongliang (57216976874); Fan, Qingwen (8316779900); Duan, Yixiang (7202190015); Xiao, Lang (59893323900)
Title: A Rectangular Toroidal Current-Based Approach for Lung Biopsy Needle Tracking
Source title: Applied Sciences (Switzerland)
Abstract: Biopsy remains the gold standard for diagnosing lung cancer, with high-quality tissue samples being critical for accurate results. To improve puncture accuracy, reduce reliance on CT imaging, and minimize procedural complications, it is essential to address the challenges of tracking the biopsy needle’s trajectory and providing real-time positional guidance to physicians. In this study, we propose a tracking model based on a rectangular toroidal current distribution to determine the biopsy needle’s relative position within the electromagnetic tracking system. A printed circuit board (PCB) is used as the platform for generating the rectangular circulating magnetic field. An alternating electromagnetic field (~70 kHz) is modeled based on the Biot–Savart law. Induced voltages from multiple transmitting coils are processed using Fourier transform algorithms to separate frequencies, enabling the independent extraction of each coil’s signal. A least squares method is employed to solve the five-degree-of-freedom electromagnetic positioning equations for the receiving coils. The objective is to establish a precise and computationally efficient electromagnetic localization model for the biopsy needle. An experimental setup simulating lung biopsy procedures is implemented, utilizing the proposed rectangular toroidal current configuration. Results demonstrate an average localization error of less than 1.76 mm, validating the effectiveness of the system in addressing the challenges of real-time biopsy needle tracking. © 2025 by the authors.
